title: http3: properly dissect CONNECT/CONNECT-UDP
description:
The http3 dissector did not follow up on the evolution
of the "CONNECT"/"CONNECT-UDP" methods, which are used for MASQUE et.al.

## Some context
The "CONNECT" method is used for tunneling other protocols on top of HTTP.
The HTTP/3 protocol is used as a building block for the MASQUE protocol,
which tunnels other protocols in QUIC `DATAGRAM` frames.

Initially, the semantics of the "CONNECT" method were grandfathered
from the HTTP/1.1 protocol:
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing the value "CONNECT"
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the host and the port.
- The `:scheme` and `:path` pseudo-headers, which MUST have been omitted.
See: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-4.3.6

When the MASQUE protocol was introduced, `draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp`
proposed a special form of "CONNECT", called "CONNECT-UDP", to allow tunneling
other protocols over QUIC `DATAGRAM` frames.
Semantics of "CONNECT-UDP" are similar to the "CONNECT" semantics above:
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing value "CONNECT-UDP" (this is the only difference from "CONNECT" above)
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the host and the port.
- The `:scheme` and `:path' pseudo-headers, which MUST have been omitted.
See:  https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp-00.html#section-3

Finally, when `draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp` has been ratified into rfc9298,
the special "CONNECT-UDP" method was deprecated in favor of the existing mechanism
known as "Extended Connect" (described in rfc8441), with the following semantics:
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing the value "CONNECT"
- The `:protocol` pseudo-header, containing the value "connect-udp" (or "connect-ip", etc.)
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the authority of the proxy.
- The `:scheme` and `:path` pseudo-headers define the target address,
  according to URI template chosen by the client.
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8441.html#section-4
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9298.html#section-2
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9298.html#section-3.4

## Changes in this MR
1. Properly parsing the different forms of the "CONNECT" message. Note that modern implementations use both the "plain CONNECT" and the "extended CONNECT" but not "CONNECT-UDP".
2. Properly constructing the target URL in accordance with the specific form of the "CONNECT*" method.
3. Fixed a typo in "CONNECT_UDP" - it is "CONNECT-UDP".
4. Fixed a bug that caused the "CONNECT" header to be appended multiple times (once when parsing `:method`, once when parsing `:authority`)

### Additional changes
1. The construction of expert information related to QPACK decoding errors is moved outside of the `if (!PINFO_FD_VISITED(pinfo)) {}` block.
2. Dropped the broken attempt to match headers that are head-of-line blocked by the QPACK stream. I will add proper support for head-of-line blocked headers later.
3. Some cleanup: formatting, removed dead code.

commits_data.message:
http3: properly dissect CONNECT/CONNECT-UDP

The http3 dissector did not follow up on the evolution
of the CONNECT/CONNECT-UDP methods, which are used for MASQUE et.al.

h1. Some context:

Initially, the semantics of the CONNECT method were grandfathered
from the HTTP/1.1 protocol:
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing the value "CONNECT"
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the host and the port.
- The `:scheme` and `:path` pseudo-headers, which MUST have been omitted.
See: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-4.3.6

Later, following the evolution of the MASQUE protocol, `draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp`
proposed a special form of "CONNECT", called "CONNECT-UDP".
Semantics of "CONNECT-UDP":
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing value "CONNECT-UDP".
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the host and the port.
- The `:scheme` and `:path' pseudo-headers, which MUST have been omitted.
See:  https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp-00.html#section-3

NOTE: before this MR, the http3 dissector attempts to dissect both
the "CONNECT" and "CONNECT-UDP" methods, but it is doing that incorrectly.

Finally, when `draft-schinazi-masque-connect-udp` has been ratified into rfc9298,
the special "CONNECT-UDP" method was replaced with the existing mechanism from rfc8441
known as "Extended Connect" (described in rfc8441), with the following semantics:
- The `:method` pseudo-header, containing the value "CONNECT"
- The `:protocol` pseudo-header, containing the value "connect-udp"
- The `:authority` pseudo-header, containing the authority of the UDP proxy.
- The `:scheme` and `:path` pseudo-headers define the target address,
  according to URI template chosen by the client.
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8441.html#section-4
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9298.html#section-2
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9298.html#section-3.4

h1. Changes in this MR

1. The values that depend on multiple header fields, such as the request URI,
   are not determined while dissecting individual fields, but moved to the end
   of the `dissect_http3_headers` function.
2. The construction of QPACK errors is moved from the `if (!PINFO_FD_VISITED(pinfo)) {}` block.
3. Dropped the broken attempt to match headers that are head-of-line blocked by the QPACK stream.
   I will add proper support for head-of-line blocked headers later.
4. Some cleanup: formatting, removed dead code.

Fixed identation

Removed the pcapng
